question.problem:
A factory machine produces defective parts with probability $30%.$ If the machine produces $6$ parts, rounded to $3$ decimal places, what is the probability that exactly $2$ or fewer of them are defective?

Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of defective parts produced.

Here, we have the following information:

- There are $n=6$ parts.

- The probability of a defective part is $p=30%=0.3.$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(6,0.3).$

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the given values into the probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{x})(0.3)^{x}(1-0.3)^{6-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{x})(0.3)^{x}(0.7)^{6-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability that at most $2$ of the $6$ parts are defective. So, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =P(X=0)+P(X=1)+P(X=2) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{0})(0.3)^{0}(0.7)^{6}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{1})(0.3)^{1}(0.7)^{5}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{6}{2})(0.3)^{2}(0.7)^{4} \\  & =1(0.7)^{6}+6(0.3)(0.7)^{5}+15(0.3)^{2}(0.7)^{4} \\  & ≈0.744,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
